info.title: tradocraft API
info.description: Business platform API (CRM, products, pricing, sales, engineering, helpdesk, customer portal).

get.summary: The identity providers: the database ones and, read-only, the one from the environment.

post.summary:
Adds an identity provider. Discovery and signing keys must be readable and the discovery
issuer must match, or the answer is 422 with the reason.

Tries a configuration without saving anything: reads discovery and keys and, with a sample
token, checks it and shows how its claims map to a user, without binding or storing anything.

put.summary:
Replaces the settings of an identity provider. Enabled providers are probed like on create.
Disabling it or changing its issuer is refused (409) when it is the last provider or the
caller's own, unless `confirm_lockout` is true.

delete.summary:
Deletes an identity provider; refused (409) for the last provider without an environment
fallback and for the caller's own provider, unless `confirm_lockout=true`. The environment
provider cannot be deleted (it is not a database row: 404).

parameters.name: confirm_lockout
parameters.description: Acknowledge that deleting can lock people out.

get.summary: The module catalogue with the company's switches.

put.summary:
Switches modules off (or on again) for the whole company. A module cannot stay on when one
it requires is switched off.

get.summary: All members of the active company, deactivated ones included.

post.summary:
Gives a person access to the company and queues an invitation e-mail. A new e-mail address
creates the user; an address that already exists (in another company) only gets the
membership and keeps its name.

put.summary:
Changes a member's name, roles, module switches and whether the membership is active.
Deactivating only affects this company. You cannot deactivate yourself or drop your own
admin role, and the company always keeps an active admin.

post.summary:
Sends the invitation e-mail again. Refused (409) once the person has signed in, because
there is nothing left to invite them to, and for deactivated members.

put.summary:
Sets or clears the identity a user signs in with, for providers with the `subject_only`
policy. The value stored is `<issuer>|<subject>`.

get.summary: The background worker's heartbeat: whether it is running, and its last outage.

parameters.name: scope
parameters.description: Only definitions of this scope (`product` or a baseline item type code).

delete.summary:
Deletes an unused definition. A definition whose key is stored on products (scope `product`) or
on baseline items of its type is refused with 409 (deactivate it with `active: false` instead,
which keeps the stored values readable).

The enabled identity providers, for the sign-in page. No sign-in needed; only these six
fields are exposed. Empty in dev mode.

Deletes an unused type. A type that has items, attribute definitions or that other types allow
as a parent is refused with 409 (deactivate it with `active: false` instead).

put.summary: Replaces the notes and lines of a draft BOM.

post.summary:
Makes a draft the active revision. The previous active revision becomes obsolete.
Refused if it would create a cycle anywhere in the product structure.

get.summary: The routing of a BOM revision: empty operations when it has none.

put.summary:
Replaces the routing of a draft BOM revision. Work centres must belong to the company and be
active, except ones the routing already uses (deactivating a work centre does not break the
routings that have it).

get.summary: Closures of all customers, e.g. to plan deliveries.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Closures that end on or after this day. Defaults to today, so past closures drop off.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Closures that start on or before this day. Defaults to no upper limit.

post.summary: Saves a configuration (with the active revision) and its evaluation.

put.summary:
Saves new inputs (and name and customer). The configuration stays on its revision unless
`revision_id` names the model's active revision (the upgrade).

delete.summary: Deletes a saved configuration. Quotations made from it stay.

post.summary:
Creates or updates the quotation of a configuration: evaluates it on its own revision
(refused while it has errors) and imports the lines with source `configurator` and the
configuration id as reference. Quoting again updates the draft quotation, or creates its next
revision once it was sent (ADR 0033).
Parses and type-checks one formula or template, for the editor.

get.summary: The functions of the formula language (for autocompletion).
The configurators of the company, with their active and draft revision.

post.summary: Creates a configurator with a first draft revision.

Imports an export as a new draft: of the configurator with the same code (409 if it already
has a draft), or of a new configurator.

put.summary: Changes the name, description, translations, product and active flag of a configurator.

post.summary: Starts a new draft revision, copied from `copy_from` or from the active revision.

get.summary: A revision with its definition and the problems that block its activation.

put.summary:
Replaces the definition of a draft. A definition with problems is saved (they are listed in
`errors`) so work in progress is never lost; it only cannot be activated. It must be a
well-formed definition document, though (422 otherwise).

post.summary:
Makes a draft the active revision (refused while the definition has problems). The previous
active revision becomes obsolete; saved configurations stay on the revision they were made with.

Evaluates a revision with the given inputs: values, visibility, lines (with their products),
issues and traces. Drafts can only be evaluated by designers (the builder's test panel).

parameters.name: language
parameters.description:
ISO 639-1 language for the product names of the lines (base names when absent or
untranslated).

parameters.description: Look ahead to this date (YYYY-MM-DD). Default: twelve months from today (at most 36).

parameters.name: language

E-mails the service report of a completed job to its contact (or the customer's main address)
and records when and to whom. Sending again is allowed. Refused (409) when there is no
address or the job is not completed.

get.summary: The signature image (PNG).

Stores the customer's signature: the request body is a PNG image. A job has one signature;
a new one replaces the old one until the service report is sent.

parameters.name: client_id

Logs time and notes of work (or travel) on a job, for the logged-in technician.

get.summary:
The jobs assigned to me that still have to be done (plus those finished in the last week),
in the order of their appointment.
Returns the match tolerances of the company.

parameters.name: id

changing anything.

put.summary: Sets the order in which rules run. The list must contain every rule of the company once.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: The team the calendar is for; without it the company calendar.

Sets the working week and time zone and switches the calendar on or off, for the company or,
with `team_id`, for one team (which then stops using the company's). Open tickets it applies
to get new due times.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: The team the calendar is for; without it the company calendar.

delete.summary:
Removes a team's own calendar and its holidays: the team uses the company's again. Open
tickets of the team get new due times.

parameters.name: team_id
parameters.description: The team the calendar is for; without it the company calendar.

post.summary:
Logs a phone call. The caller is looked up by phone number; the call is added to the given
ticket, or a new ticket is opened for it.
Imports a raw e-mail (RFC 5322, e.g. a saved .eml file) as if it had arrived in the mailbox.

get.summary: The mailboxes of the company, the default one first.

delete.summary:
Removes a mailbox. Its tickets and e-mails stay; replies on them then leave through the
default mailbox.

get.summary:
The helpdesk report for a period. Response and resolution times are in business time when the
ticket's own calendar (its team's, else the company's) is on (see `basis`). Days are the
company's local days.

notice can still go out for an open ticket that is late when its rule is switched on.
Replaces the windows for the given priorities. Open tickets get new due times.

then the earliest day, then the slot that leaves the least unused time in its gap. Slots lie
inside working hours, outside absences and keep the travel buffer to other jobs.

value.description:
A string, number or boolean; an array for `in`; ignored for `is_null` and `not_null`.
Dates are `YYYY-MM-DD`, also for date-time fields (compared as UTC days).

On a date or date-time field the value may instead be a relative date, an object that is
resolved against today each time the report runs (so a saved report stays live):
`{"relative": "<token>"}` with the token `today`, `yesterday`, `this_week`, `last_week`
(weeks start on Monday), `this_month`, `last_month`, `this_quarter`, `last_quarter`,
`this_year` or `last_year`; or `{"relative": "last_n_days", "n": 30}` (the 30 days up to and
including today) and `{"relative": "next_n_days", "n": 7}` (today and the 6 days after),
with `n` from 1 to 3660. Each token is a range of days. `eq` matches the whole range, `ne`
everything outside it; `gte` and `lt` compare with the first day, `gt` and `lte` with the
last day (`gte last_month` is "from the start of last month", `gt last_month` is "after
last month", `lte` and `lt` the other way round). For a single day (`today`,
`yesterday`) all operators therefore read naturally. Not allowed with `in`, `is_null` and
`not_null`, or on other field types.

subtotals above, which cover product lines only. The server always sends it; the schema marks

marks it optional so clients tolerate an older server, where an absent value means unknown.

consumed_quantity.description: Already shipped or consumed from this allocation.

quantity.description:
The quantity that should be reserved for the line in total, in the stock unit of the
product. More reserves additional stock, less releases the newest allocations, 0 releases all.

warehouse_id.description: Take additional stock only from this warehouse...

force.description:
Reverse even when that takes stock that is reserved for orders (they then lack stock).
Inventory administrators only, which this endpoint already requires.

id.description: Chosen by the client for the reversal move.

errors.description: Problems that block activation; empty when the definition is valid.

run_minutes_per_unit.description: Minutes for each unit built, in the stock unit of the product.

setup_minutes.description: Minutes once per production order, whatever its quantity.

RowError.description: One problem in an import file.

column.description: Column name; null when the problem concerns the whole row.

row.description: Line in the file where the row starts (the header is line 1).

stop_on_match.description: Later rules are not looked at when this one matched.

RuleAction.description:
One change a rule makes. `kind` decides which of the other fields is used:
`set_owner` (`user_id`), `set_team` (`team_id`), `set_priority` (`value`), `set_category`

period_hours.description: `send_email`: at most one mail per ticket and rule in this many hours (default 24).

RuleChange.description: A change a rule made (or, in a dry run, would make).

RuleConditions.description:
What a ticket must look like for a rule to apply. Every given condition has to hold; a list
holds when the ticket has any one of its values. Empty conditions match every ticket.

customer_languages.description: The language of the customer (nl, fr, en, de, es).

sender_domain.description: The part of the contact's address after the `@`, case-insensitive.

ids.description: Every rule of the company, in the wanted order.

changes.description: The changes that actually change the ticket (actions that change nothing are left out).

SalesSuggestion.description: A product worth adding to the quotation or order. Never blocking, never added automatically.

because_of_code.description: The product on the quotation that triggered the suggestion.

SalesWarning.description: A hint about a line that never blocks anything.

details.description:
Machine-readable details: `status` (incompatible | needs_external_supply | unknown_grid),
`country_code`, `supported` and `available` profiles. For `incompatible_products`:
`product_codes` (the pair), `note` and `relation_id`.

shared.description: Share with everyone in the company who may run reports.

technician_ids.description: Replaces the technicians of the job.

oneOf.description: The job after the change.

SerialComponent.description: A serialised component in the current as-built tree, depth-first.

bom_id.description: BOM revision the unit was built to. Default: the product's active BOM, if any.

customer_id.description: Required for delivered and installed, unless the unit already has a customer.

status.description: in_stock | delivered | installed | scrapped (built_in is set by attaching to another unit)

parent_id.description: The unit this one is currently built into.

warranty_status.description: in_warranty | expired | unknown (no end date recorded)

warranty_until.description: The end of the warranty, if known.

serial_unit_id.description: The serial unit the repair is about.

token.description: The token from the login link.

default_job_minutes.description: Length assumed for a job without an end time.

timezone.description: Time zone of working hours and absences, e.g. `Europe/Brussels`.

travel_buffer_minutes.description: Minutes kept free between two consecutive jobs of a technician on the same day.

auth_mode.description: `dev` (the admin e-mail becomes the dev user) or `oidc` (sign in through the identity provider).

needs_setup.description: True while no company exists and bootstrapping is enabled on this server.

carrier.description: Sets the carrier and tracking reference as part of shipping.
Carrier chosen; keeps the one entered when marking the request as requested.

currency.description: Must equal the quotation currency. Defaults to it.

usage.description: How it is written, e.g. `round(x, digits?)`.

ack_enabled.description: Send an acknowledgement (ticket number and target response time) on creation.

breach_enabled.description: Send a notice when the first response time has run out without an answer.

priority.description: low | normal | high | urgent. Absent: every priority.

rules.description:
The most specific rule wins: team and priority, then team, then priority, then neither.
A ticket that matches no rule gets no notice.

compliance_percent.description: Share of tickets that did not breach, 0-100.

tickets.description: Tickets with a service level that were created in the period.

article_ids.description: The messages (articles) that move to the new ticket. At least one, and not all of them.

subject.description:
The subject of the new ticket; default: the subject of the first moved message, else the
subject of this ticket.

probability.description: Defaults to the stage's default probability.

StockMove.description: One row of the ledger, as shown to staff.

entered_quantity.description: What the user typed, when it was in another unit than the stock unit.

reversed_by.description: The move that reversed this one.

seq.description: Position in the ledger; moves are shown newest first by this number.

unit.description: The stock unit the quantity is in.

unit_cost.description:
Cost per stock unit: what the posting module booked, else the standard cost of the product
at the time of the move. Only with `inventory.cost`.

StockRow.description: Stock of one product at one location and lot.

available.description: On hand minus reserved; negative when stock was adjusted away from reservations.

StoredError.description: One problem of an import, as stored with the job and shown to the person.

column.description: The column the problem concerns; null for the row as a whole.

row.description: Line (CSV) or sheet row where the problem is; the header is at its own row.

because_of_code.description: The product of the set that triggered the suggestion.

confidence.description: 0 to 1, share of the orders with the other product that also contain this one.

SuggestionOut.description: A suggestion as the API returns it.

SupplierProduct.description: A supplier price list entry for a product.

TargetState.description: What one target (first response or resolution) looks like at `now`.

at_risk.description: Not breached, not met yet and less than 25 % of the window is left.

breached.description: The due time passed before it was met (or, if still open, it has passed).

due_at.description: When it is due; empty when the ticket has no service level (internal tickets).

met_at.description: When it was met (first response sent, ticket closed).

minutes_remaining.description: Whole minutes left (negative when overdue). Empty once the target is met.

client_id.description:
Chosen by the client: sending the same id again returns the first task instead of adding a
second one (offline retries). The same id with another description is a 409.

members.description: The complete member list: members not listed are removed.

anchor_date.description: The first due date; defaults to the start of the contract.

id.description: Give the id of an existing template to change it; without one a new template is made.

category.description: question | lead | quote_change | order_confirmation | production_question | service | complaint | other

contact_id.description: The person at the customer this ticket is about (see the contacts of the customer).

csat_rating.description: The customer's latest satisfaction rating: good | bad.

escalated_at.description: Set when a colleague escalated the ticket by hand.

language.description: nl | fr | en | de | es — the language to answer in.

merged_into_id.description: Set when this ticket was merged into another one (it is closed).

sla.description: Due times, breach flags and minutes remaining.

suggested_category.description: What the system guessed from the last incoming e-mail.

team_id.description: The queue the ticket waits in (the owner is the person working on it).

unread.description:
For the caller: there is activity by others since they last read the ticket and they are

watching.description: For the caller: they follow the ticket. Filled like `unread`.

readers.description: Colleagues who opened the ticket, most recent first ("seen by").

TicketInput.description: Full update of the ticket's fields and links.

TicketSla.description: The SLA of a ticket as the API shows it.

paused.description: The clock is stopped: the ticket waits for the customer.

state.description: none (no service level) | on_time | at_risk | breached

actor_user_id.description: The colleague (events, notes, replies) or the customer's name (incoming messages).

comment.description: Events: the internal reason or comment. Messages: the first 300 characters.

from_value.description: status / priority: the old value; merged: the number of the merged ticket.

kind.description:

tag_added | tag_removed. Messages: email_in | email_out | note | call_in | call_out | portal_in.

to_value.description:
status / priority: the new value; assigned: `owner` or `team`; tags: the tag;

complete_children.description:

open.description: Open root items on my plate (the list the page shows by default); sub-items are not counted.

overdue.description: Open root items on my plate that were due before today (the database date).

assignee_id.description: Hands the item to a colleague. Not allowed for sub-items.

client_id.description: Chosen by the client; a repeated create with the same id returns the item that exists.

position.description: Defaults to the end of its siblings.

assignee_id.description: The colleague the item is handed to; absent when it stays with the owner.

mine.description: Whether the caller is the owner (only the owner reassigns and deletes).

parent_id.description: The root item this is a sub-item of; absent for a root item.

assignee_id.description: Owner only; cascades to the sub-items.

oneOf.description: What a sign-in would do; only for a valid token.

reason.description: Why the token is not valid.

signature_ok.description: The signature verified with a published key.

rule_path.description: JSON path of the rule in the definition.

values.description: The names the rule's formulas read, with their values.

category.description: unit | weight | length | area | volume | time

generate_on.description: The day the job is (or was) generated.

closure_override_reason.description: Needed to plan on a closed day when the policy is `override`.

expected_updated_at.description: The `updated_at` of the note as it was loaded; refused (409) when the note changed since.

lines.description: Replaces all lines; omitted keeps them.

oneOf.description: Replaces the ship-to address; omitted keeps it.

calculated.description: What the formula gives, when the value is pinned.

options.description: Allowed values (choices, product pickers, alternatives of an overridable value).

duplicates.description:

message.description: What is wrong, in words, when `status` is `bad_format` or `bad_checksum`.

reason.description:

The address split as well as it can be: street lines, postal code and city. Absent parts

period.description: The day, or the Monday of the week.

assigned_user_id.description: The technician a service van belongs to.

warranty_until.description: The last day of the warranty; empty when unknown.
